Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the Indian second innings. Smriti Mandhana will be taking the strike with Shafali Verma as her partner on the other end. Darcie Brown will be opening the attack for Australia Women.
... THIRD INNINGS ...

The task ahead for India - With a 125-run deficit to erase, the Indian batters enter a critical phase of the match where survival will be the top priority. The primary goal will be to navigate the treacherous pink ball under lights and reach the end of the day with minimal damage. If they can see out this testing period, they will hope to post a substantial target on Day 3 to put the Aussies under pressure. However, with Australia firmly in the driver’s seat, it will be a true test of character for the visitors to stay in the contest. We will be back soon.

India’s Bowling Effort - India’s bowlers showed flashes of brilliance throughout the innings, led by Sayali Satghare, who finished with impressive figures of 4 wickets for 50. Kranti Gaud and Deepti Sharma provided vital breakthroughs with two wickets apiece, while Sneh Rana and Shafali Verma chipped in with one each. India now faces a daunting task as they head into the twilight session, where the pink ball is expected to dart around under the lights.

Sutherland’s century and the tail-tend surge - The standout performance of the innings belonged to Annabel Sutherland, who converted her solid start into a magnificent 129. Her century was the backbone of the Australian total, highlighted by disciplined stroke play and excellent strike rotation. Following her departure, crucial lower-order contributions from Alana King and Lucy Hamilton ensured the momentum wasn't lost, pushing the team past the 300-run mark. Australia Women were eventually bundled out for 323, securing a significant 125-run first-innings lead.

The Perry-Sutherland rescue - Australia’s pursuit of India’s 198 began on shaky ground as the Indian seamers exploited the early movement to leave the hosts reeling at 58/3. However, the momentum shifted dramatically through a masterful 128-run partnership between Ellyse Perry and Annabel Sutherland. Perry played a composed and vital knock of 76 to steady the ship, while Sutherland took control of the innings, anchoring the crease with authority. Their clinical association not only erased the early deficit but firmly placed the pressure back on the Indian bowling attack.

India are starting with spin in the form of Sneh Rana. Oh, a change of mind from Harmanpreet Kaur. Sayali Satghare will start with the ball. Lucy Hamilton will face the first ball. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Bright sparks, but not enough - It has been a hot day out in Perth and India Women have toiled hard for two sessions now. In the first session, their catching let them down big time and they went behind the eight ball. The bowling was much better in the second session on Day 2 as the spinners bowled long spells. The medium pacer Sayali Satghare, though, has been the pick of the bowlers and has picked up a couple of wickets, just as Kranti Gaud and Deepti Sharma. Even though there's the difficulty of batting under the lights, India need to clean things up with the ball at the earliest. Right then, Australia Women currently lead by 112 runs. How far can they stretch that? Will India be able to clean things up early after the break? Even if they do, how will they perform with the bat under lights? A lot of questions, and we should get all the answers in the post-Dinner session. Do join us at 3.50 pm IST (10.20 am GMT) for all the action.

Let's now hear from the centurion herself - Annabel Sutherland says it was pretty good out there and adds that it is a lovely place to bat once you are set. She mentions that it was nice to build a couple of good partnerships in the middle. Sutherland also shares that it was really special to have her parents watching on from the stands. She hopes Australia can add a few more runs to the total before letting the bowlers do the job. Shares that there is still plenty in the wicket, which is exciting for the bowling group.

Australia in command - Even after losing plenty of wickets in the session gone by, the hosts are well in control of this contest. The lead is beyond the 100-run mark, which is a crucial milestone, and even if they get bowled out early in the final session, Australia won't mind it as they will get to bowl with the new ball under the lights. The highlight of the session was yet again Annabel Sutherland's batting, and she went on to convert her fourth score of 50-plus into the century, so she currently has 4 Test centuries and no fifties, in just 7 matches as well. Ashleigh Gardner and Tahlia McGrath probably should have done a bit more, but the likes of Alana King and Lucy Hamilton have ensured that the visitors are made to toil a bit more in the field.

Time for a Dinner break - SESSION SUMMARY - 30 overs, 93 runs and 4 wickets. A well-fought session and after reducing Australia Women to 277/8, India Women have failed to stop the lead from going beyond the 100-run mark, thanks to a 33-run unbeaten stand between Alana King and Lucy Hamilton. And this partnership has put the Aussies in a commanding position heading into the final session on Day 2.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the WACA. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of India Women. Annabel Sutherland and Beth Mooney are all set to resume their stay at the crease as well. Sneh Rana to continue after the break as well. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Looking ahead - Annabel Sutherland also received a lifeline towards the end of the session, with Richa Ghosh dropping a tough chance when she was on 90. Whenever Sutherland has gone past fifty in Test cricket, she has converted it into three figures, and she looks well on course to do that today as well. In these energy-sapping conditions, Harmanpreet Kaur will have to be mindful of her pacers and is likely to use them in short, sharp bursts. We could see the visitors begin the second session with pace after the break as they look to make inroads into this Australian lineup. The post-Tea session will commence at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT). See you then. Cheers!

A quick word with Australia's star all-rounder - Ellyse Perry notes that batting with Annabel Sutherland made scoring easier during their crucial partnership, helping to navigate tricky twilight conditions on Day 1. Perry indicated that while the pink ball moved significantly under lights, daylight offered better opportunities to rotate strike and find boundaries. Looking ahead, she emphasised the team's intention will be to bat for a long time and push for the win afterwards.

India strike but Australia hold firm - The tourists eventually managed to break the 128-run stand, and there could have been another quick one for the visitors soon after, but Beth Mooney was given a reprieve by Sneh Rana. Mooney had not even opened her account then. Rana and Deepti Sharma subjected her to a thorough interrogation, sticking to tight lines and lengths, but Mooney managed to weather that spell and saw Australia through to the end of the session.

Perry and Sutherland led the Aussie charge - There was enough in the wicket for the pacers early on, with a bit of movement through the air as well, but the Indian seamers were inconsistent. Whenever they erred, Perry and Sutherland made sure they capitalised, keeping the scoreboard ticking at a healthy rate. In the process, Perry went past Karen Rolton's tally of 1002 Test runs to become Australia's most prolific run-getter in the format. Harmanpreet Kaur soon turned to spin from both ends, but it was a similar story for the spinners as well, as they struggled to hit the right areas consistently.

That will be TEA - 121 runs were scored in the session from 31 overs. Australia began the day trailing by 102 runs but now find themselves with a 19-run lead, which they will look to extend in the sessions to follow. India managed just a solitary wicket in the session. While they will take some heart from the way they managed to pull back the scoring rate after dismissing Ellyse Perry, they will also reflect on the chances that went begging.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going on Day 2. It is bright and sunny as Harmanpreet Kaur leads her troops out to the middle. They are followed by the two overnight batters, Ellyse Perry and Annabel Sutherland. Kashvee Gautam will kickstart proceedings with the ball. Perry to face the first ball of the day. Justin Langer expects the wicket to get better to bat on as the day goes on. Here we go!

The battle continues - The first two sessions of Day 2 are expected to be the most batter-friendly, and Australia will be desperate for Perry and Sutherland to capitalize on this window to overhaul India's lead. Conversely, India knows that the ball will do less in the bright daylight, making it imperative for their bowlers to maintain strict lines and continue chipping away at the Australian wickets. If the Indian seamers can find early breakthroughs, they can keep themselves firmly in this contest, if not, Australia could quickly take the game away. An enticing battle between bat and ball is about to resume.

The twilight challenge - Australia's response began under the treacherous twilight period, where the pink ball famously comes alive. Indian debutants Sayali Satghare and Kranti Gaud exploited these conditions brilliantly, reducing the hosts to a nervous 58/3. Satghare made a dream start by bowling out Georgia Voll and later dismissing the Australian captain, Alyssa Healy. However, the ever-reliable Ellyse Perry is unbeaten on 43, and the in-form Annabel Sutherland managed to weather the storm, stitching together an unbroken 38-run partnership to ensure no further damage before the close of play.

Indian batting struggles on Day 1 - India's first-innings total of 198 was a story of missed starts and relentless Australian pressure. Jemimah Rodrigues provided the lone substantial resistance with a composed 52, but the top order struggled to contend with the swing and seam of the pink ball. Australia's Annabel Sutherland was the chief destroyer, bagging 4/46, while 19-year-old debutant Lucy Hamilton made an immediate impact with 3 scalps to her name. A late-order flourish from debutant Kashvee Gautam helped push the score close to 200, but India will feel they left plenty of runs on the table on a surface that rewarded batters if they hung in there.

Sunshine strategies - Welcome back, cricket fans, to what promises to be a gripping Day 2 of the Pink Ball Test. Day 1 was a masterclass in pace bowling as 13 wickets tumbled at the WACA, and 12 of them went to the pacers' account. India Women were bowled out for 198 after a disciplined Australian attack took full advantage of the conditions. While India's total seemed modest, their bowlers struck back brilliantly under the lights to leave Australia at 96/3 by stumps. Trailing by 102 runs, the Aussies will look to Ellyse Perry and Annabel Sutherland to exploit the friendlier batting conditions of the second day, while India aims to maintain their momentum and keep this high-stakes contest wide open.

See you tomorrow - As Day 1 ends, Australia is firmly in the driver's seat. We'll be back with the action for Day 2, with the first ball scheduled for 5.20 am GMT. Make sure to tune in early as we bring to you our pre-match build-up before the action resumes. Until then, it's goodbye from the commentary box! Cheers.

Aussies struggled under lights as well - Batting under the twilight floodlights is famously difficult with the pink ball, and the Indian bowlers tried to take advantage. Debutant Sayali Satghare bowled a beautiful delivery to remove Australian opener Georgia Voll early on. Kranti Gaud and Satghare kept the pressure high, grabbing two more wickets, including captain Alyssa Healy, to leave Australia slightly nervous at 58/3. Despite the wobble, the experienced Ellyse Perry and all-rounder Annabel Sutherland stepped up to rescue the Australian innings. They calmed things down, batted sensibly, and made sure their team didn't lose any more wickets before the close of play. The Australian scorecard currently reads 96 for 3 after 27 overs. They currently trail by 102 runs with 7 wickets in their bank.

India's innings ended at 198 runs - When play resumed under the artificial lights, Australia quickly finished the job. India Women were bowled out for a disappointing total of 198 runs in just 62.4 overs. Annabel Sutherland was the star of the innings, taking 4 wickets, while the young debutant Lucy Hamilton impressed everyone by picking up 3 wickets.

Jemimah steadied the ship - The middle session, leading up to the Dinner break, brought more trouble for India as Annabel Sutherland took charge of the Australian bowling attack. Jemimah Rodrigues was the standout player for India, showing great composure to score a solid 52 runs before playing a loose shot. Despite some late resistance from the lower-order debutants, India slipped further to 184/8 by Dinner.

Early wickets for Australia - India endured a very rocky start to their innings. Australian debutant Lucy Hamilton made an immediate impact by bowling star opener Smriti Mandhana for just 4 runs. Shafali Verma tried to counter-attack with a quick 35, and captain Harmanpreet Kaur added an aggressive 19, but Australia kept striking at regular intervals. By the Tea break, India were struggling at 99/4.

A tricky start - Australia Women are on top at the moment. They won the toss in this Day-Night Pink Ball Test at the WACA. In a special milestone moment, it was Australian captain Alyssa Healy's final toss in international cricket, and she wisely chose to bowl first. The decision paid off almost immediately as the Australian bowlers put the Indian batting lineup under heavy pressure from the start of the Indian inings.
